title: Eleanor Weekender — Old Money — Nine Ad Storyboards

cards.text: ELEANOR WEEKENDER — OLD MONEY — NINE AD STORYBOARDS

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Three aspirational fashion openings × Anna, eurofall-weekender-C3 and mer-oldmoney-C1. Each hook displays four distinct coveted Birkin-style designer bags; Eleanor does not appear until its named introduction. The desired outcome is the old-money silhouette without the designer expenditure. Existing shared Weekender footage and approved narration remain. No on-screen text; timing provisional.
H1 · Designer cost

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Everyone wants that old money look until the bag costs more than the trip.
Four coveted Birkin-style designer bags: black grained leather with cream tailoring; golden tan on walnut; taupe with navy trousers; burgundy on an ivory chair.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Desire — makes the coveted old-money silhouette tangible in four distinct finishes. Let the voice carry the price contrast while the picture stays aspirational.

Latest direction: four different coveted Birkin-style bags, no Eleanor and no problem/solution comparison. Separate existing avatar layer. First product reveal is C01. Still storyboard plate; no motion rendered; no on-screen text.
H2 · Outfit transformation

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Before you buy another outfit to get that old money look, try changing your bag.
Four Birkin-style bags paired with four desirable outfits: chocolate/white shirt/jeans; ivory/knit/charcoal; navy/camel coat; gray/black blazer/silk skirt.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Style identification — the silhouette is the recurring taste cue across four already-polished outfits. Invites the viewer to imagine styling it with their own wardrobe.

Latest direction: four different coveted Birkin-style bags, no Eleanor and no problem/solution comparison. Separate existing avatar layer. First product reveal is C01. Still storyboard plate; no motion rendered; no on-screen text.
H3 · Travel style

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: You planned the perfect airport outfit. Don't let your beat-up travel bag ruin it.
Four travel-wardrobe Birkin-style bags: black with rolling luggage; saddle on hotel bench; taupe at porte-cochere; olive on an elegant train seat.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Travel aspiration — four desirable designer bags express the polished travel wardrobe the viewer wants. Beautiful accessories carry this hook, without damaged-bag agitation.

Latest direction: four different coveted Birkin-style bags, no Eleanor and no problem/solution comparison. Separate existing avatar layer. First product reveal is C01. Still storyboard plate; no motion rendered; no on-screen text.

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: LATEST DIRECTION — OLD-MONEY DESIRE
cards.text: The audience covets the Birkin silhouette and wants that style without the designer expenditure. Hooks show four different beautiful designer-style bags. No Eleanor in a hook; no failed solutions, battered bags, price-shock faces or before/after. Presenter bridges lead to the named Eleanor introduction. No text anywhere in ad footage.

cards.title: VOICE — EXACT REQUEST
cards.text: Woman Over 40 · ElevenLabs Eleven V3 · Creative. Stability 0.0; similarity 0.85. Raw friend-to-friend read: natural breaths, varied emphasis, no announcer cadence or forced rasp. One continuous take per hook, shared across its three avatars. Audio generation and audible quality review are pending.

cards.title: HOW TO READ THE BOARD
cards.text: Nine ads = three complete sequences × three existing avatars. Start with the hook previews and avatar roster, then the nine combinations. Each H1/H2/H3 sequence continues left-to-right through its numbered sections. All approved words are preserved. A1 previews stand in for the selected avatar on presenter-only cards.

cards.title: NO SCREEN TEXT + LAYERING
cards.text: All nine ads: no on-screen text. No subtitles, captions, hook headlines, comparison labels, product titles or CTA overlays. 9:16; avatar approximately 30–35% width at the grid intersection, clear of faces, handles and hardware. Keep the chosen identity throughout.

cards.title: EDIT + SOUND
cards.text: Aspirational designer grids open each ad; cut to the presenter at the bridge, then reveal Eleanor at C01. Direct cuts follow spoken cues. Dry raw voice forward; optional restrained music. No comparison edits, shocked reactions or on-screen text. Align timing to final voice.

cards.title: CTA + END HOLD
cards.text: Final line names the Eleanor Weekender in the voice only. Hold the clean product image for 1.2 seconds after the last word. No CTA text, titles, sale or scarcity graphics. Existing end-frame plate is selected on C13.

cards.title: EXISTING B-ROLL
cards.text: Shared coverage uses the existing Weekender library; no new common-body B-roll. All bridges hold on the presenter. Travel and mirror inserts appear once in each body at C02/C03. Cross-ad reuse is intentional. Older brand library images are generated assets, not documentary customer footage.

cards.title: ASSET REVIEW
cards.text: Three new designer-bag grids inspected: four different desirable all-leather bags per grid, no Eleanor canvas/oval hardware, no visible text or reaction/comparison scenes. These are generated Birkin-style editorial depictions. Existing body excerpts preserve Cognac Weekender design; physical scale unverified. Motion QA remains for production.

cards.title: PRODUCTION HANDOFF
cards.text: Board delivers hook first frames, existing avatar previews, selected B-roll frames, exact scripts and edit decisions. Google Omni for hook motion when producing; existing HeyGen identities with selected ElevenLabs audio; isolated DaVinci Resolve timeline after connection check. New voice, lip-sync and final exports are not part of this storyboard delivery.
